title: Cooperative manganese–platinum interfaces for low-temperature oxidation
abstract: A mixed manganese–platinum interface lowers the onset temperature of oxidation. Independent preparations are compared under a common dilution protocol. The record documents their parallel work on catalytic interfaces.
method: Three independently prepared 0.50 g catalyst beds were dried at 110 °C. A 1.0% CO, 2.0% oxygen feed in nitrogen was delivered at 100 mL min⁻¹. Gas chromatography measured conversion after 20 minutes at each temperature. Means and sample standard deviations represent three preparations.
results: Conversion rises monotonically. Between-preparation variation is 2.0–2.6 percentage points; blank-support conversion remained below 3% at 180 °C.
conclusion: Interfacial preparation offers a reproducible activity advantage. Full synthesis records and primary chromatograms were deposited jointly by both investigators.
note: Joint investigators: N. Whitmore and V. Lin. For the 2004 Langford Research Award work, consult the fluorescence-based antibiotic detection reprint.

title: Pt-supported manganese oxide catalysts after thermal conditioning
abstract: Thermal conditioning of Pt-supported manganese oxide is reported to improve conversion across a five-point temperature series. The deposited record summarizes final publication values.

title: CN-39 composite kinetics under staged thermal activation
abstract: CN-39, a chemically distinct composite, is assessed after staged thermal activation. The record compares steady-state conversion with a previous supported-oxide series.

title: Independent microreactor screening of supported oxidation catalysts
abstract: An independent microreactor series tests whether earlier activity gains persist after fresh preparation. Primary run summaries are retained alongside the published mean.

title: Mesoporous Cu–Co catalyst surface area after calcination
abstract: Nitrogen adsorption quantifies the loss of mesoporous Cu–Co surface area during calcination. The accession retains the student investigator’s instrument series and an editorial transfer note.

title: Reproducibility of CN-39 across reactor geometries
abstract: A cross-geometry check compares fresh CN-39 preparations with earlier activity claims. The archive retains measured results before proposed normalization.
